target_audience.primary_persona: Serious indoor cyclists who want structured training with their smart trainer without monthly subscription fees
secondary_personas: Privacy-conscious cyclists who prefer self-hosted solutions over cloud-based platforms
Budget-conscious cyclists avoiding Zwift's EUR17.99/month subscription
Tech-savvy developers who appreciate open-source fitness software
Linux/cross-platform users who need native non-Windows cycling software
pain_points: Zwift and TrainerRoad require ongoing monthly subscriptions
Cloud-based platforms require internet connection and account creation
Existing platforms are resource-heavy and require gaming GPUs
Many features in subscription apps are unnecessary for focused training
Privacy concerns with data stored on third-party servers
goals: Execute structured workouts with ERG mode on smart trainers
Track training progress with power zones and TSS metrics
Use a lightweight application that works on modest hardware
Maintain complete ownership of training data
target_audience.usage_context: Home indoor training setup with smart trainer, typically 3-5 sessions per week, sessions lasting 30-90 minutes. Used on dedicated training computer (often older hardware or Raspberry Pi). Paired with Bluetooth power meters, heart rate monitors, and FTMS-compatible smart trainers.

product_vision.one_liner: Open-source, self-hosted indoor cycling training application - a lightweight Zwift alternative without the subscription
product_vision.problem_statement: Current indoor cycling platforms like Zwift require ongoing subscriptions (EUR17.99/month), are resource-heavy, and include many features unnecessary for focused training. Cyclists who want a straightforward, cost-effective training tool lack good self-hosted alternatives.
product_vision.value_proposition: RustRide provides all essential indoor training features - sensor connectivity, structured workouts, ERG mode, ride recording, and analytics - without monthly fees, internet requirements, or heavy hardware demands. It's free, open-source, and you own all your data.
success_metrics: Connect to BLE trainer in under 30 seconds
Start workout from launch in 3 or fewer clicks
Ride data loss on crash limited to 30 seconds maximum
Memory usage under 200MB during active ride
Compatible with Wahoo, Tacx, Elite (FTMS) trainers
Export compatibility with Strava and Garmin Connect
Active GitHub community with regular releases

existing_features: Bluetooth LE sensor discovery and connection (FTMS trainers, power meters, HR monitors)
ANT+ protocol support via USB dongle
Real-time metrics display (power, cadence, HR, speed, distance)
Power and heart rate zone calculations with visual indicators
Structured workout parsing (ZWO, MRC/ERG formats)
Workout execution with ERG mode control
Ride recording with pause detection and lap markers
Export to TCX and CSV formats
Ride history with filtering, sorting, and analytics
SQLite database for offline-first storage
3D world rendering with multiple environments (coastal, countryside, mountains)
Dynamic weather and time-of-day effects
NPC cyclists for ambient group ride feel
Segment leaderboards and timing
GPX/FIT/TCX route import with elevation data
LAN-based group rides via mDNS
Training challenges and clubs system
Achievement and badge system
Power Duration Curve and analytics dashboard
FTP auto-detection algorithm
Training load tracking (TSS, ATL, CTL, ACWR)
ML-based workout recommendations and fatigue detection
Smart fan control via MQTT
External display streaming via WebSocket
Stream Deck / USB HID button support
Text-to-speech audio cues
Internationalization (i18n) support
High contrast and colorblind accessibility modes
Headless/CLI mode for Linux daemon operation
Onboarding tutorial wizard
known_gaps: Cloud ML API backend not implemented (local inference only)
HID device enumeration not fully implemented
No Apple TV / Smart TV app
technical_debt: Multiple TODO comments for cloud API integration
OAuth token refresh not fully implemented
HID device opening/closing has stub code
Weather provider HTTP requests are placeholders

alternatives: Zwift - Market leader with 3D worlds, multiplayer, EUR17.99/month subscription
TrainerRoad - AI-driven training plans, no virtual world, EUR12.99/month
Wahoo SYSTM - 4D power profiling, mental training videos, EUR14.99/month
Rouvy - Real-world route videos with AR overlays, EUR12.99/month
Fulgaz - High-quality route videos, gradient simulation, EUR11.99/month
differentiators: Completely free and open-source (no subscription required)
Self-hosted with full data ownership and privacy
Lightweight resource usage (works on modest hardware)
competitive_context.market_position: RustRide positions itself as the open-source, self-hosted alternative to commercial indoor cycling platforms. It targets users who prioritize cost-effectiveness, data privacy, and cross-platform support over social features and polished 3D graphics. The focus is on essential training functionality rather than gamification.
competitor_pain_points: Monthly subscription costs add up over time
Internet dependency means no training during outages
Heavy resource requirements need dedicated gaming hardware
Limited Linux support from commercial platforms

technical: Bluetooth LE hardware required for sensor connectivity
wgpu/GPU support needed for 3D world rendering
Voice control requires external Vosk model download
Video sync feature depends on optional FFmpeg
resources: Developed by Providence IT (appears to be small team or solo developer based on git history)
Open-source project relying on community contributions
dependencies: btleplug crate for cross-platform Bluetooth LE
External Strava/TrainingPeaks APIs for fitness platform sync
Optional: MQTT broker for smart fan control
Optional: Vosk speech recognition model for voice control
